FXUS65 KPSR 092336
AFDPSR

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Phoenix AZ
435 PM MST Fri Oct 9 2026

.UPDATE...
Updated Aviation

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...

- Generally dry conditions along with temperatures around 10 degrees 
above normal will persist today.

- An Extreme Heat Warning remains in effect for western Imperial 
County and Yuma through this evening. 

- An unsettled pattern will take shape this weekend along the West 
Coast and drag the remnants of Tropical Cyclone Rachel into the 
Southwest United States, resulting in heightened chances for showers 
and thunderstorms, widespread gusty winds on Sunday, and much cooler 
temperatures.


&&

.SHORT TERM /TODAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
Fairly quiet conditions will round out the work week before several 
weather systems interact to bring unsettled and regionally impactful 
rain, wind, and severe weather potential over the weekend. Today, 
the influence of broad anticyclonic flow remains over the Desert 
Southwest, with H5 heights analyzed between 584-586 dam at this 
hour. Though heights are gradually eroding today, thermal profiles 
have yet to respond meaningfully, and thus 850 mb temperatures 
upwards of 24C-26C (above the 90th percentile of climatology) will 
continue to support highs around 10F above daily normals. Yuma and 
El Centro will once again be within a couple of degrees of daily 
records, with areas of Major HeatRisk still continuing. Therefore, 
Extreme Heat Warnings remain in effect for the Imperial Valley and 
Yuma areas through this evening. 

Over the Eastern Pacific, Tropical Storm Rachel and a subtropical 
shortwave/cutoff low have begun to interact well offshore the 
Northern Baja Peninsula, turning the tropical system's track 
northeastward. South southwesterly moist flow will increase in 
earnest Saturday and especially by Saturday night, with NAEFS mean 
IVT near/exceeding climatological maximum for this time of year. 
Moisture and upper level support are likely to peak Saturday 
night/early Sunday morning as the remnants of Rachel quickly eject 
northeastward near/along the Lower Colorado River, resulting in the 
most widespread coverage of showers and storms. However, before the 
peak timing for rain chances, scattered showers and thunderstorms 
are expected to erupt as early as late Saturday morning/Saturday 
afternoon. Strong, gusty winds and localized heavy rainfall remain 
the main threats with this initial activity. SPC has issued a 
Marginal risk for severe storms Saturday into early Sunday morning, 
and indicates at least a very low chance for a tornado or two. The 
strengthening wind fields do support this, with GFS bufr soundings 
also showing a brief window with higher MUCAPE (upwards of 500-1000 
J/kg), EBWD 30-40 kts, SFC-1 km shear above 10 kts, and LCLs 
lowering below 2000 m. Supercellular storms modes do look like they 
will be supported by the environment, at least for a temporary 
window of time Saturday night into Sunday morning. However, it is 
important to keep in mind this is a highly volatile forecast, with 
small upstream changes resulting in large downstream forecast 
shifts. Regardless, with any organized storm modes that develop 
Saturday PM into Sunday, the primary and more widespread threat will 
be for damaging wind gusts. 

&&

.LONG TERM /SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...  
The more impactful weather is expected on Sunday as the remnants of 
Rachel move through. According to the latest official forecast track 
from the National Hurricane Center, Rachel is expected to accelerate 
north-northeastward along the vicinity of the Lower Colorado River 
Valley. An area of heavy rainfall is likely to follow along and just 
to the west of where Rachel tracks. Even though the official NHC 
forecast has the system tracking along the vicinity of the Lower 
Colorado River Valley suggesting that the heavy rainfall may fall 
across portions of southeast CA, there is a lot of spread amongst 
the guidance in the track as some solutions have Rachel tracking 
near the southern CA coast whereas other solutions have the system 
tracking as far east as southwest AZ. Therefore, the rainfall 
forecast is still highly volatile and could still significantly 
shift depending on the eventual track. The greater impact with 
Rachel will be the potential for strong  winds as a belt of strong 
850 mb winds in excess of 40-50 kts is likely to set up along the 
eastern quadrant of Rachel with much of the guidance showing gusts 
exceeding 40-50 mph across much of southwest into south-central AZ, 
especially early Sunday morning through Sunday afternoon. Wind gusts 
this high could certainly result in areas of blowing dust across the 
dust prone areas. Given the strong wind potential, a wind advisory 
has been hoisted from eastern Riverside and Imperial Counties 
through all of southwest and south-central AZ. In addition to the 
wind threat, there will also be the potential along the eastern 
quadrant for multiple rounds of widely scattered showers and storms 
to materialize. There is a potential for some of these storms to 
reach severe levels given that strong vertical shear in excess of 50 
kts will be present, however, the severe potential will be dependent 
on how much instability will be present. 

Even though the remnants of Rachel will be well north of the area by 
Sunday evening, unsettled conditions will continue right through 
early next week as the main west coast trough moves through the 
region bringing additional chances for showers and isolated 
thunderstorms, with the highest chances across the foothills and 
higher terrain areas to the north and east of Phoenix from upslope 
flow. Thereafter, drier and quieter weather is expected by the 
middle of the week as the main trough axis lifts to the northeast. 

Under the presence of the troughing pattern, well-below normal 
temperatures are expected during the first half of next week with 
lower deserts highs going from the low to mid 80s on Sunday to 
mostly 70s Tuesday and Wednesday. Early morning lows will also take 
a tumble with the coolest morning expected on Wednesday as 
temperatures are expected to bottom out in the 50s across much of 
the region with even some 40s across the higher terrain areas. 

&&

.AVIATION...Updated at 2335Z.

South Central Arizona including KPHX, KIWA, KSDL, and KDVT:
The primary weather issue will be SHRA moving into the area Saturday 
afternoon as midlevel cigs thicken and lower. Confidence in wind 
direction early this evening is low, generally oscillating 140v200 
until reverting back to an E/SE component. Cigs will also develop in 
a 10-15K ft AGL layer with widespread virga developing, which could 
locally affect wind speeds and directions briefly. Winds should 
maintain a SE trajectory Saturday, however SHRA entering the area in 
the afternoon may create erratic directions. Coverage of SHRA 
appears low enough to preclude a predominant mention, and will 
advertise a prolonged period of VCSH. A few embedded TSRA will also 
be possible, but odds only justify a prob30 mention at this time. 

Sunday outlook: High impact weather still appears to be arriving at 
all terminals Sunday mid/late morning through the afternoon. 
SHRA/TSRA should surge into the area with gusty south winds and 
MVFR/IFR cigs. The lower cigs and TSRA threat should be rather short 
lived over a 3-4 hour window late morning through early afternoon 
before lifting out of the aerodrome space. However, very strong S/SW 
winds will fill in behind the SHRA with gusts 35kt or higher 
throughout the afternoon. 


Southeast California/Southwest Arizona including KIPL and KBLH:
Showers moving into the area Saturday morning and afternoon with 
thick midlevel cigs will be the main weather issue this TAF period. 
Confidence is very good that winds will swing from a southerly 
direction to more of a W/SW direction through the evening as midlevel 
cloud deck begin to increase. Scattered SHRA will begin to move into 
the region Saturday morning as cigs lower to around 10K ft AGL, 
though coverage only dictates a VCSH mention. While an isolated TSRA 
is possible, odds are too low to include in this TAF package. Far 
more impactful weather will arrive after the TAF time frame Saturday 
night through Sunday afternoon. 

&&

.FIRE WEATHER...
A much more unsettled weather pattern will develop over the weekend 
as increasing moisture associated with the remnants of Tropical 
Storm Rachel brings increasing rain chances. The chances for showers 
and storms increase starting Saturday afternoon/evening and 
continues into Sunday with a greater than 50-70% chance of wetting 
rainfall area wide. Winds will also increase significantly, 
especially late Saturday night through Sunday with widespread gusts 
exceeding 30-40 mph. With the increasing moisture and cooler 
temperatures, MinRH values will increase from 25-40% Saturday to 45-
70% on Sunday along with good to excellent overnight recoveries. 
Another weather system will bring additional chances for wetting 
rainfall early next week, mainly for the eastern districts, before 
quieter weather settles in by the middle of the week. 

&&

.CLIMATE...

Record highs:

----     ----     ---------
Oct 9 106 in 2024104 in 1996

&&

.PSR WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
AZ...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM MST this evening for AZZ532.

     Wind Advisory from 2 AM to 5 PM MST Sunday for AZZ530>533-535-
     536.

     Wind Advisory from 8 AM to 5 PM MST Sunday for AZZ534-537>563.

CA...Extreme Heat Warning until 8 PM PDT this evening for CAZ566-567.

     Wind Advisory from 2 AM to 5 PM PDT Sunday for CAZ560>570.

&&

$$

SHORT TERM...Whittock
LONG TERM...Lojero
AVIATION...18
